cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3). God asks what the people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge'. So Dad eats the sour grapes, and the CHILDREN are the ones making the face?

cards.question: True or false: God says the people of Israel will keep on quoting the sour grapes proverb.
Before God settles the sour grapes question, He says every soul belongs to someone. Who?
Every soul, father and son, belongs to God. And God says the soul who sins will die for its ___ sin.

cards.text: Now God walks through one family. First, suppose a man is righteous: he doesn't eat at the mountain or look to idols, doesn't defile his neighbor's wife, doesn't oppress anyone, doesn't rob and doesn't take excess interest.

cards.question: Instead of robbing anyone, this righteous man shares what he has with people in ___.
This righteous man follows God's statutes and faithfully keeps His ordinances. True or false: God says he will surely live.

cards.text: Now suppose that righteous man has a violent son who sheds blood. Same kitchen, COMPLETELY different batch: this son eats at the mountain, robs, oppresses the poor and needy and lifts his eyes to idols.

cards.question: True or false: Because his father was righteous, the violent son will live.

cards.text: God answers His own question: 'Will this son live? He will not!' Now that violent man has a son of his own, and that son has a front-row seat to every sin his father commits.

cards.question: The violent man's son sees all the sins his father commits. What does he do with what he sees?

answers.text: Thinks it over and does not copy it
Copies his father one sin at a time
Tries to make up for it with offerings

cards.text: So this son stays away from idols, doesn't rob, feeds the hungry and keeps God's ordinances, and God says he will surely live. That's watching your coworker hit reply-all to the WHOLE company, thinking it over, and saying, 'Nope. Not me.'

cards.question: True or false: The violent father will still die for his iniquity, even though his son did not follow in his steps.

cards.text: Then God says the people may ask, 'Why shouldn’t the son bear the iniquity of his father?' Friend, that's like asking why you didn't get the parking ticket for somebody else's car.

cards.question: Why does God say the son who didn't copy his violent father will surely live?

answers.text: He did what is just and right
He moved away from his father

cards.text: Then God comes back to it: 'The soul who sins is the one who will die.' And He spells it out: a son won't bear his father's iniquity, and a father won't bear his son's.

cards.question: God says a person's righteousness or wickedness will fall upon someone. On whom?

cards.text: Good or wicked, it lands on the one who did it. Nobody else's name goes on your cookie box.
Now God flips it around. Suppose a wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all God's statutes and does what is just and right.

cards.question: True or false: A wicked man who turns from all his sins and does what is just and right will still die for the sins he committed before.

cards.text: None of the transgressions he committed will be held against him. Not. One.

cards.question: Then God asks whether He takes any pleasure in the death of the wicked. What would He prefer for the wicked man?

answers.text: That he turns from his ways and lives
That he pays for every one of his sins
That he stays far away from Israel

cards.text: But it works the other way too. Suppose a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits the same abominations as the wicked.

cards.question: A righteous man turns away and starts doing what the wicked do. What happens to all the righteous acts he did before?

answers.text: None of them will be remembered
They cancel out his new sins
They protect his children from harm

cards.question: True or false: The righteous man who turns to the abominations of the wicked will still live.
God says the people of Israel say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' True or false: God turns it around and asks if it's Israel's ways that are unjust.

cards.text: So God lays it out again: the righteous man who turns to iniquity will die because of it. But the wicked man who considers and turns from all his transgressions will surely live.
And the house of Israel says it AGAIN: 'The way of the Lord is not just.' And God turns it back on them again: 'Are My ways unjust, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unjust?'

cards.question: Then God tells the house of Israel how He will judge them. How?

answers.text: By the deeds of their kings

cards.question: God calls the house of Israel to repent and turn from all their transgressions. Why?

answers.text: So their iniquity won't be their downfall
So the priests will accept their offerings
So their enemies will leave them alone

cards.question: God tells the house of Israel what to do with all the transgressions they have committed. What?

cards.text: He tells them to fashion for themselves a new heart and a new spirit. Then He asks them straight: 'Why should you die, O house of Israel?'
And His last word: 'For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, declares the Lord GOD. So repent and live!'
